completion_data.completion_summary: Relocated the --meta, --review, and --dream telemetry sub-modes from the memory extension's /distill surface into a new core-owned /telemetry command backed by skill-telemetry across five phases: authored five new core files, registered them in core's manifest/index/README/CLAUDE.md, repointed every cross-extension guardrails/meta-spec citation, retired the three sub-modes from memory's /distill (now nine sub-modes), and redeployed plus verified all three live end to end against this repo's real event and prompt-history data.

memory_candidates.content: When an implementation phase's own plan carries a 'Scope Hypothesis' asserting a specific count of files/citations, always re-run the grep immediately before editing rather than trusting the stated number -- it caught two real discrepancies in this task (a plan undercounting a file's own citation references by one, and an uncertain 'provides.context already covers patterns/standards' claim that turned out true but needed live verification). Report any discrepancy explicitly rather than silently absorbing it into a wider or narrower edit.

During a multi-task /orchestrate batch, an intermediate (non-final) implementation phase declaring Verification Tier: full can hit the same severe gate-8 contention the dispatch's Batch Gate Deferral section anticipates for the plan's literal final phase -- one single meta-test (test-gate-cache-equivalence.sh) was observed running 10+ minutes under concurrent sibling load. When ps aux confirms genuine heavy concurrent verify-deploy.sh/run-all.sh activity from other dispatched tasks, applying the same scoped-tier-plus-deferral treatment by analogy to an intermediate full-tier phase (not just the literal final one) is a reasonable, explicitly-recorded deviation -- run the narrowest --only-gate selection that covers the phase's own touched files, defer the rest, and record the reasoning as both an issue-log entry and a progress-file deviation.

After deleting source-store markdown files that have deployed copies AND removing their index-entries.json entries, a single deploy-headless.sh redeploy pass may leave the deployed .claude/context/index.json aggregate still carrying 'ghost index row' findings for the removed entries, even after the orphaned deployed .md files themselves are explicitly removed. A second redeploy pass (after the explicit orphan-file removal) correctly regenerates the aggregate index.json fresh and clears the ghost rows. Plan for two redeploy passes when a phase both deletes source files and prunes their index entries in the same dispatch.
